title: False discovery rate of Benjamini-Hochberg
ask: BENCHMARK. The protocol's grid has axes named `m`, `pi1` and `method` (with the values none, bonferroni and bh) and includes the setting m = 200, pi1 = 0.2, with at least 500 repeats per setting. Declare a metric with id `fdp` (kind mean; one value per repeat: the false discoveries divided by the discoveries, 0 when there are none).

answers.source: for independent continuous p-values Benjamini-Hochberg's FDR is exactly pi0 * alpha = 0.8 * 0.05 (Benjamini & Hochberg 1995; Benjamini & Yekutieli 2001)
